gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the ePropulsion eLite and kLite 750 cannot run directly from an external battery. Their Range Extension Kit only lets a 12 V third-party battery recharge the built-in 378 Wh pack at up to 100 W. The Spirit 1.0 Plus does take external batteries directly (39–60 V input), and the new 44 V Torqeedo Travel batteries are not on the compatibility list of the older 29.6 V Travel 1003/1103 battery.
standout_why: Pages compared: the cited ePropulsion eLite page, the cited Torqeedo Travel S page, the Torqeedo Travel results ChatGPT got and sparkpowered.com. The eLite page names the 'kLite/eLite Range Extension Kit for Third-Party Batteries (KL-AC01-00)' as an accessory, but it doesn't say what voltage the kit takes, that the motor can't run from that battery, or the 100 W limit. The Travel S page lists only 'Travel Battery / Travel Battery XP / No Battery' and never mentions the older 915 Wh pack. Sparkpowered gives only the general advice that 'most portable outboards only take their own' batteries and names no model. I could not check three rival pages: yachtandocean.com (404), trollingmotorsdirect.org (TLS certificate error) and the device.report chart (403).
decides: This settles which 'motor with battery' setups can actually use a separate battery. A shopper who buys a kLite 750 or eLite and adds a 12 V LiFePO4 battery (for example the Redodo 12V 50Ah we already list) gets a slow on-water recharger, not more power. ePropulsion's own extended-range figure is 378 Wh + 691 Wh = 1,069 Wh, and the external battery flows in at no more than 100 W, so refilling the 378 Wh pack takes at least 3.8 h. A shopper who wants to swap in a bigger separate battery should look at the Spirit 1.0 Plus, whose external-battery input accepts 39–60 V and for which ePropulsion recommends its E-Series packs. Owners of an older Torqeedo Travel 1003/1103 should not expect their 915 Wh battery to carry over to the new Travel S, because the new packs are 44 V. The traditional 12 V Redodo batteries on our page do not plug into any of these integrated motors.

findings.label: Running from an external battery
findings.value: Not supported. The motor runs only from its integrated 378 Wh battery
findings.note: Page quote: 'The kLite 750 is powered by its integrated battery and cannot be operated directly from an external battery.'

findings.label: Range Extension Kit: battery and charge rate
findings.value: 12 V third-party batteries; up to 100 W charging input through the charging port
findings.note: Page quotes: 'The eLite/kLite Range Extension Kit is compatible with 12V third-party batteries' and 'The kit connects through the charging port and can provide up to 100W of charging input'. The page sends readers to the owner's manual for recommended battery specs. Arithmetic: 378 Wh ÷ 100 W ≥ 3.8 h to refill the built-in pack from an external battery, before conversion losses.

findings.label: Maker's extended-range figure
findings.value: 378 Wh integrated + optional 54 Ah (691 Wh) = 1,069 Wh total
findings.note: The page doesn't state the 54 Ah battery's chemistry. 54 Ah × 12.8 V = 691.2 Wh, which matches a 12.8 V nominal (LiFePO4-class) battery; that is my inference. The page's base runtimes were tested 'without a solar charger or range extender'. AC charger 100–240 V included, about 4 h from 0%; 12 V charger optional.

findings.label: Third-party battery accessories
findings.value: kLite/eLite Range Extension Kit for Third-Party Batteries (KL-AC01-00); optional 12 V charger (EL-C002-00); optional solar charger (EL-C003-00)
findings.note: The eLite page lists the kit but not its supported batteries. Its integrated battery is 378 Wh at 25.2 V lithium-ion, and it has a USB-C output.

findings.label: Solar-charger-to-battery cable
findings.value: EL-AC06-00, 1,500 mm, 'Compatible with the eLite Solar Charger, third-party batteries to easily extend the range of your eLite / kLite 750'
findings.source_title: eLite Solar Charger to Third Party Battery Cable Kit - ePropulsion parts database
findings.note: The parts page gives no battery voltage, type or price.

findings.label: External battery support
findings.value: Yes. Input 39–60 V; ePropulsion recommends E-Series batteries (E40, E60, E80, E100, E163, E175) via the Spirit 1.0 Plus/Evo External Battery Cable 1.5 m (00-0601-08)
findings.note: The page's spec table says 'Yes, and E-Series Battery recommended' for external batteries on the Plus, Evo and Evo Remote. The standard battery is the Spirit Battery Plus, 1,276 Wh. Charge time is 8.5 h standard and 3.5 h fast.

findings.label: Compatible battery (current generation)
findings.value: Travel Battery 1,080 Wh, 44 V nominal, 8.3 kg; 'Compatible with: Travel XS / Travel. Compatible but reduced motor power with Travel XP'; $1,599.00
findings.note: The Travel S page sells the motor for $1,799.00 and the Travel Battery for $1,599.00, or both as the Essential Package for $3,398.00. A 180 W mains charger is included, and the solar cable ($99) handles panels up to 200 Wp.

findings.label: Larger battery option
findings.value: Travel Battery XP 1,425 Wh, 44 V nominal, 9.6 kg, 'Compatible with: Travel / Travel XP', MSRP $1,899.00
findings.note: This is Torqeedo's US B2B page.

findings.label: Older battery and its compatibility list
findings.value: Battery 915 Wh, 29.6 V, 31 Ah, 'Compatible with Travel 503/603/903/1003/1103'; $1,199.00; currently not available
findings.note: The list doesn't include the Travel S/XP. It is a 29.6 V pack, while the new Travel S packs are 44 V. Torqeedo's pages state no explicit exclusion either way.
